items.title: AI is Already Everywhere in Publishing
items.excerpt: Book Riot's podcast unpacks the Wired expose on publishers' internal AI use and yet another prize-winning story suspected of being AI-written, arguing AI is already embedded across the publishing workflow.

items.title: Why Are Publishers Suing Big Tech With One Hand and Embracing AI With the Other?
items.excerpt: After an Authors Guild panel on authorship and AI, a Lit Hub writer examines the contradiction of publishers litigating against AI companies while rolling out generative tools in-house.

items.title: About that Wired article on book publishers “quietly” using AI
items.excerpt: Jane Friedman flags an under-the-radar detail: publishers say the number of authors using LLMs to write their books is much higher than reported.

items.title: PayAuthors.com: Are your books in pirate libraries?
items.excerpt: PayAuthors.com is a new website and service that lets authors check whether their books appear in pirate libraries used to train AI models.

items.title: Thélyson Orélien denies using AI to write novel but admits to plagiarism in earlier work
items.excerpt: Canadian author Thélyson Orélien denied using AI to write his prize-winning novel C'était ça ou mourir, but admitted to 'unacceptable' plagiarism in earlier work.

items.title: Quebec author accused of using AI gives up proving novel's origins, publisher says
items.excerpt: Orélien has abandoned the effort, disclosed by his publisher Éditions du Boréal, to document how his novel was written amid AI-authorship allegations. (Off-list: new development not yet covered by on-list outlets.)

items.title: SoA's position on generative AI 'remains unchanged' after backlash to Ethical AI Charter
items.excerpt: Society of Authors CEO Anna Ganley responded to member criticism of its newly released Charter of Ethical AI Use in the Creative Industries, saying the body's stance on generative AI has not changed.

items.title: Toniebox 'will never become AI toy', CEO Tobias Wann tells FBF
items.excerpt: Tonies CEO Tobias Wann said the kids' audio company has experimented with AI for some products but 'will never become an AI toy'.

items.title: Guest Post – Artificial Intelligence in Scholarly Publishing: Are We Moving Faster Than the Evidence?
items.excerpt: A guest post argues the next phase of AI adoption in scholarly publishing workflows needs more evaluation, collaboration and human judgment.

items.title: Halo's co-creator wrote a novel about AI taking over the world
items.excerpt: Bungie co-founder Jason Jones has written a novel about AI taking over the world; The Verge runs an excerpt chapter.

items.title: Korean, Japanese, Taiwanese books targeted in Anthropic's 'Project Panama' hunt for AI training material
items.excerpt: Shipping and court records show Anthropic sourced vast quantities of Asian-language books for AI training, widening the Korean copyright row to Japan and Taiwan.

items.title: [단독] 구글도 韓 책 구매한다는데…AI 학습 저작권 강화 법안 ‘낮잠’
items.excerpt: 앤트로픽에 이어 구글도 국내 출판사를 상대로 도서 구매 계약을 추진하는 것으로 나타났지만, AI 학습 저작권을 강화하는 법안은 국회에서 멈춰 있다.

items.title: [AI돋보기] AI 시대에 귀해진 '인간의 글'…헌책방 뒤지는 빅테크
items.excerpt: 최첨단 AI를 개발하는 빅테크 기업들이 학습용 '인간의 글'을 확보하려 낡은 종이책과 헌책방에 눈을 돌리고 있다.

items.title: 스포티파이·아마존…테크 기업, 세계 최대 도서전 몰려온 까닭
items.excerpt: 프랑크푸르트 도서전의 최대 화두는 AI로 제작비를 낮춘 오디오북이었고, 스포티파이·아마존 등 테크 기업이 모든 책을 듣는 책으로 만드는 새 먹거리에 몰려들었다.

items.title: I'm 'under threat' because AI thinks Black writers aren't human
items.excerpt: After Caine Prize winner Simbarashe Kundizeza was accused of using AI, a writer describes how AI detectors and suspicion are falling disproportionately on Black writers. (Off-list: first-person angle not covered on-list.)

items.title: Fish Audio Launches Drama 3 to Direct AI Voices and Edit a Single Word
items.excerpt: Fish Audio's Drama 3 TTS lets producers direct AI voice performances in plain language and re-record a single mis-stressed word, pitched at audiobook and audio-drama production. (Off-list: maker-side narration tool absent from on-list feeds.)
